findings.title: retrieved.add(taskId) outside catch block — failed tasks counted as retrieved, masking errors in poll_summary
findings.suggested_fix: Add a failedCount counter inside the catch block. Move retrieved.add(taskId) inside the try block after event emission succeeds, or keep it outside but add poll_summary.failed_count to distinguish 'attempted but errored' from 'retrieved with data'.
findings.why_it_matters: When googleOrganicTaskGetAdvanced throws, the catch logs and execution falls through to line 247. retrieved.size reaches totalTasks even if all tasks errored; timed_out=false; status='active' with events=[]. Caller has no signal that anything failed.
evidence: Line 242-245: catch logs error. Line 247: retrieved.add executes unconditionally.
Test line 349: asserts poll_summary.retrieved===2 even when task2 returned HTTP 500.

findings.title: Task POST response mapped to original queries by array index, not by tag — wrong metadata if API reorders entries
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the tag field from the POST response entry to reconstruct the original query, rather than relying on taskList[i] to chunk[i] positional alignment. Alternatively build a Map keyed by 'keyword|location_code|language_code' from the submitted tasks and look up by those fields in the response.
findings.why_it_matters: If DataForSEO returns response entries in a different order than submitted (e.g. due to per-task validation errors shifting positions), taskIdToQuery binds the wrong ValidatedQuery to a task ID. All emitted events for that task carry wrong keyword/country_code/language_code metadata.
evidence: Lines 161-165: for loop maps by index i. chunk[i] is the submitted query at position i.
Line 155: tag set to 'keyword|country|lang' but never used in lines 161-165.
DataForSEO API does not guarantee response order matches submission order when per-task errors occur.

findings.title: estimatedSpendUsd computed from inputs.length before locale validation and batch cap — overstates actual spend
findings.suggested_fix: Move the estimatedSpendUsd computation to after line 126 (after capped is defined) and use capped.length * (baseCostPerTask + 0.0006). This gives the actual number of tasks that will be POSTed.
findings.why_it_matters: inputs.length includes locale-rejected and batch-capped queries that never reach the API. When DATAFORSEO_MAX_BATCH_PER_RUN is set low or many locales are unsupported, the estimate can be significantly higher than actual spend.
evidence: Lines 101-111: locale validation reduces to valid.length.
Line 126: batch cap reduces to capped.length.
estimatedSpendUsd is never recomputed after these reductions.

residual_risks: Poll ceiling is a soft limit: the while condition at line 180 is checked at loop top only. One full iteration (sleep up to 120s + tasksReady fetch + N sequential taskGetAdvanced fetches) can overshoot pollCeilingMs by the sum of those network times. With 500 tasks ready in one round, actual wall time can substantially exceed the 10-minute ceiling.

lookupDataForSeoLocale falls back to the bare country key at line 29. If a multi-language country ever gets a bare key added to dataforseo_location_map.json (currently clean — no bare BE/CH/CA keys exist), that fallback would silently return the wrong language for requests that specify a non-default language for that country.
testing_gaps: No test where ALL tasks fail googleOrganicTaskGetAdvanced — would surface that status='active', events=[], poll_summary.retrieved===total, timed_out=false with no error signal. The existing per-task error test (line 316) only covers partial failure (1 of 2 tasks fails).
No test for POST response returning fewer entries than the submitted chunk size — partial positional alignment path (taskList.length < chunk.length) is untested.
